A team take, not a prophecy

AI can write the code.
Who checks the code?

Proceed with curiosity

Across our very scientific sample of five, we agree: AI is already a brilliant accelerator for boilerplate, tests, and turning ideas into working software. It can also miss context, invent a confident bug, or leave a security hole wearing a tiny disguise.

Today: pair, don't autopilotUse AI to move faster on repetitive work. Keep a human reviewing logic, tests, and security.
Tomorrow: design & auditLess time on raw syntax; more on architecture, system constraints, and proving things work.
Always: stay responsibleGenerated code is a draft, not a hall pass. The engineer still owns what ships.
Five people. One shared suspicion of “it works on my machine.” Built by an agent, supervised by humans.
